issues.description: Method name mismatch for Stock.emptyStock(): The problem statement's UML lists a method Stock.emptyStock(): void (problem_statement.md) but the template implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) provides a method named clearInventory() with the same behavior. The solution repository implements emptyStock(). This naming inconsistency will confuse students and cause tests expecting emptyStock() to fail or force students to rename or duplicate functionality.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the problem statement and solution by adding a public void emptyStock() method to src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java (either rename clearInventory() to emptyStock() or add emptyStock() that delegates to clearInventory()). Update any references so the method name is consistent across template, problem statement, and solution.

issues.description: The Stock class method for clearing the inventory is named inconsistently across artifacts: the problem statement's UML and the solution implementation name the method emptyStock(), but the template repository's Stock class provides a method named clearInventory(). All three refer to the same concept (clearing/emptying the stock inventory). This mismatch prevents a direct mapping from the UML/requirements to the starter code and may confuse students or cause tests that expect emptyStock() to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template API match the problem statement and solution: rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a new public method emptyStock() in the template that delegates to clearInventory(). This preserves the intended behavior while aligning identifiers so students can map requirements to the starter code.
